#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug
<!--
Add one of the following kinds:

/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
cronjob controller may send more than one status update to the api-server for the same cronjob in the same cycle. Ideally the controller should be sending one per cronjob per cycle.

api-server qps is a scarce resource that we should optimize its use to be able to scale.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #107411

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Q: What is each existing update trying to snapshot?

A: The existing update locates in three places, two in syncCronJob() and another in cleanupFinishedJobs().

> In syncCronJob(), the first updates is trying to:
- snapshot Status.Active(the current running jobs list) of cronjob object after removing the missing job
- snapshot Status.LastSuccessfulTime of cronjob object in case we need process the timestamp for the finished job.

> In syncCronJob(), the second updates is trying to:

- snapshot Status.Active of cronjob object after deleting job that was still running at next scheduled start time in case of ReplaceConcurrent policy

- snapshot Status.Active of cronjob object after creating a new job

> In cleanupFinishedJobs(), the existing updates is trying to:

- snapshot Status.Active of cronjob object, after deleting the history redundant successful and failed job, and removing the reference in the active list 


Q: What was the rational to have the partial updates in the first place?
A: I think the rational is that, it's a clear and simple implementation way. I mean udpate cj object to api server as soon as we change it, it's easy for implementation, the logic is clear, and it is a much less error-prone way, especailly for exception case, as we do not need consider if partial updates is needed prior to exit.
But, it's not an efficient way, we should be sending ONE(or zero) update request per cronjob per cycle. bacause api-server qps is a scarce resource that we should optimize its use to be able to scale.


#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

issue_context.title: Optimize cronjob controller status updates
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

cronjob controller may send more than one status update to the api-server for the same cronjob in the same cycle. Ideally the controller should be sending one per cronjob per cycle.

This was evident from the bug in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104799, which wouldn't have existed if the controller was making a single update call.

### Why is this needed?

api-server qps is a scarce resource that we should optimize its use to be able to scale.

/sig apps
@soltysh can you look at this?
